issues.issue: Did the Federal Court wrongly hold that some section 16 positions need proof of actual influence, despite the binding Adam decision?
issues.applicant_position: Adam is binding: a senior public service position under s.16(d) is deemed senior; no factual inquiry into actual influence is needed.
issues.result_quote: The decision in Adam was a binding precedent on the Federal Court, and the Court erred in failing to follow Adam.

issues.issue: Did the Federal Court properly depart from prior top-half decisions on senior public service positions?
issues.applicant_position: The Federal Court ignored conflicting top-half decisions without giving cogent reasons to depart from them.
issues.respondent_position: Respondent highlighted the military top-half approach (Sekularac); its position on civil public service posts is not stated.
issues.result_quote: the Federal Court erred in law by failing to reference these prior, conflicting decisions

issues.issue: Was the visa officer's reading of prescribed senior official, using the top-half test, a reasonable interpretation?
issues.applicant_position: The officer's reading fits the text, context and purpose of the Act and Regulations, including s.42.1; it was reasonable.
issues.result_quote: the officer’s interpretation of the legislation was one that the legislation could reasonably bear

issues.issue: Was it reasonable to find Kassab a senior member of the Iraqi public service despite his claimed lack of influence?
issues.applicant_position: His posts were senior, some three levels below Saddam Hussein; influence need not be shown, so the officer's finding was reasonable.
issues.respondent_position: Kassab said his Catholic faith, non-Ba'ath membership and informal restrictions meant he lacked real influence or benefit.
issues.result_quote: In my view it was reasonable for the visa officer to conclude that the respondent was a senior member of the Iraqi public service

issues.issue: Does the top-half test properly set the limits of senior members of the public service?
issues.applicant_position: No argument was made on appeal on whether the top-half test properly sets these limits.
issues.respondent_position: No argument was made on appeal on this point; the Federal Court did not deal with it.
issues.result_quote: this is a question to be answered in a case when it is raised on the facts and considered by the Federal Court.

issues.issue: Must a broader analysis of actual ability to influence be done once a senior position in a designated regime is shown?
issues.applicant_position: Holding a senior reporting-hierarchy position suffices; a broader analysis of ability to influence is not required.
issues.result_quote: A broader analysis into the individual’s ability to benefit or exert influence is not required in this circumstance.
